business: MyLiquid app (an AI agent with a Tamagotchi-style pet that invests and pays within your limits)
by_segment: Busy delegator (uses a robo-adviser or nothing)
why_not: Right now it's demo money, and the real version has no named broker and no price, so there's nothing real to sign up for. I'm not putting my paycheck behind an AI pet from an app I've never heard of.

I'd probably play with the free demo pet on my commute because I love keeping a streak going, but signing up to pay for an AI to move my real money is different. I've got less than $20k saved and nobody is telling me who covers it if the agent messes up.

I already put the same amount into index funds every month for free in my broker app and barely look at it, so paying a monthly fee for an agent to do roughly the same thing just eats into my returns. The pet is cute, but I'm not paying a subscription to invest.

The pet is cute and I'd probably keep a streak going on the free demo, but I'm not paying a monthly subscription on top of my investments when my robo-adviser already does the rebalancing for me. A waitlist for a paid plan with no price yet isn't something I'd sign up for on my commute.

I already ask ChatGPT what to do and then make the trades myself, and my broker is rolling out its own AI for free. I don't see why I'd pay another monthly fee for a cartoon pet to do something I can already do without paying.

I already paste my questions into ChatGPT for free and my broker is rolling out its own AI stuff, so I don't see why I'd pay a monthly fee and move my money to some partner broker I've never heard of. Putting in a few hundred every payday by hand takes me five minutes.

I put the same amount into index funds every month and don't look, and that already works fine. A cartoon pet that trades and rebalances for me is the opposite of what I want from my money: boring, set-and-forget, and nothing to babysit.
